title: Streaming chat event gateway and idempotent ack model
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: the Python SDK streaming chat surface emits raw server events (delta tokens, meta events, heartbeat) with inconsistent envelopes across transport variants (SSE / websocket / long-poll). Consumers repeatedly reimplement glue code for deduplication, idempotent acknowledgment, resumability, and backpressure shaping. This ticket introduces a first-class Event Gateway and an idempotent ack model in the Python SDK to provide a single ergonomic primitive for building resilient streaming chat consumers and examples for common patterns.

Scope: implement EventGateway and Acknowledger classes in the Python SDK core; provide an opt-in resumable session token persisted by the application; expose hooks for user telemetry, metrics, and backpressure signals; and ship three canonical examples (simple consumer, resumable consumer, and ack-backed exactly-once sink). Not in scope: server-side protocol changes or new backend storage for checkpoints (we will rely on user-provided storage adapter interface).
acceptance_criteria: EventGateway consolidates SSE/WS/HTTP streaming events into a single typed iterator that yields (event_type, payload, seq, resume_token)
Acknowledger supports idempotent ack semantics: ack, nack, and at-least-once checkpoints with stable resume_token generation
Backpressure hooks allow consumers to signal desired concurrency/buffer sizes and the gateway honors load-shedding when internal queue limits are reached
Three example notebooks/snippets are added to the SDK docs demonstrating (1) basic streaming consumer, (2) resumable consumer with persisted checkpoint, (3) ack-backed exactly-once sink pattern
Unit and integration tests cover envelope normalization, duplicate suppression, resume token validity across reconnects, and ack semantics
API is backwards-compatible: existing streaming convenience helpers still work but can be wired through the gateway without user changes
implementation_notes:
Core additions: EventGateway class (transport adapters + normalizer), Acknowledger interface (methods: ack(seq), nack(seq), checkpoint(seq) -> resume_token), StorageAdapter protocol for durable resume_token storage. Transport adapters implement a common contract: connect(), iter_events(), graceful_close(). Use a fixed-size asyncio.Queue as internal buffer; expose .pause()/.resume() callbacks to propagate backpressure to transport adapter. Provide a lightweight in-memory default StorageAdapter for quickstarts and tests. Avoid changing public StreamingClient surface; implement gateway as opt-in middleware. Use type stubs and detailed docstrings so the new primitives are discoverable in IDEs.

Tradeoffs considered:
- Persisting resume state server-side would simplify UX but requires backend changes and migrations — deferred.
- Stronger exactly-once guarantees (distributed transactions) are out of scope; we provide ack-backed idempotence and guidance.
- Using Redis as the only storage adapter would be easier to test at scale but would bias users; instead we publish an example RedisAdapter in examples repo.
progress_updates: 2025-01-16: Tech spike completed — prototype gateway that normalizes SSE + WS to common event tuples. Spike code in PR #3110 (experimental).
2025-01-20: Design doc uploaded and reviewed by Platform Infra; main concerns: resume token entropy and collision risk. Added HMAC salt suggestion to design doc.
2025-01-23: Implemented initial EventGateway + in-memory StorageAdapter in feature branch feature/gateway-981234. Basic unit tests added for envelope normalization.
2025-01-28: Design review — PM asked for sample notebook showing failure recovery with reconnects. Added example plan and estimate +2 points.
2025-01-30: Opened PR 3124. CI failing on integration test for WS reconnect sequence ordering; investigating race in transport adapter reconnection logic.
2025-02-03: Fixed race by introducing reconnect backoff and drain-before-reconnect in transport adapter; integration test now stable locally. Preparing for internal review.

test_plan: Unit tests: envelope normalization, resume_token encoding/decoding, ack/nack semantics, backpressure pause/resume. Integration tests: SSE+WS end-to-end with simulated reconnects and duplicate delivery; flaky scenarios run under stress with pytest-xdist. Load test: lightweight harness that runs 10k short-lived clients against the gateway adapter to validate memory/queue behavior. Example-driven tests: run example scripts in CI integration stage to assert expected resume behavior after simulated failures.
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind SDK runtime flag `ENABLE_EVENT_GATEWAY`. Stage 1: internal dogfood in Redwood Console (10% of internal teams) for two weeks. Stage 2: opt-in public beta via pip release with docs and examples. Stage 3: graduate to default in next minor release if no critical issues. Communicate breaking changes and upgrade guide in SDK CHANGELOG.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: resume_token collisions could lead to cross-session duplication — mitigation: include client-instance id + HMAC-signed nonce in resume_token. Risk: increased memory pressure in long-lived processes — mitigation: default small queue sizes and a configurable eviction policy; document guidance. Risk: users misuse ack model leading to data loss — mitigation: add clear examples, enable verbose debug telemetry by default in beta.
docs_and_examples: Create three example notebooks under docs/examples/streaming: 1) basic_consumer.py, 2) resumable_consumer_with_redis.py, 3) ack_backed_sink_example.py. Update SDK reference: EventGateway and Acknowledger sections with code snippets and migration notes for existing streaming helpers.
owner_notes: Next steps: finish PR feedback loop, add RedisAdapter example, expand CI integration to include WebSocket proxy with induced packet loss. Schedule a short sync with design + infra to confirm HMAC key rotation approach.
